newsitem.title: DENMARK: GN Store Nord to double turnover by 2000.
newsitem.headline: GN Store Nord to double turnover by 2000.

text.p: Danish cable and telecoms group GN Store Nord on Tuesday set a target to double turnover by 2000, with pre-tax profits rising yearly by at least 15 percent.

"It is our aim to maintain and improve our competitiveness and double net turnover by the year 2000, with pre-tax and extraordinary items profits rising by a minimum of 15 percent every year until that date," GN Store Nord said in a statement.
It listed its 53.5 percent-owned Sonofon mobile telephony unit, which competes with market-leader Tele Danmark on the Danish domestic market, as one of the six key operations it intended to focus on.

It said it expected a lower profit before tax and extraordinary items for 1997's first six months than the 1996 interim period's 121 million crowns, but that the full year result would show a 250 million crown surplus, 15 percent up on last year's 213 million crowns.
GN Store Nord's group turnover was 2.722 billion crowns in 1996.
It said it planned a 700 million to one billion crown share issue this autumn, with half of the proceeds earmarked for new investment in Sonofon.
GN Store Nord is due to announce its interim 1997 result on August 28. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
